newsitem.title: USA: New Yorker denied bail in alleged killing of mother.
newsitem.headline: New Yorker denied bail in alleged killing of mother.

text.p: The son of a wealthy doctor whose body was found in the trunk of her luxury car more than two years ago was denied bail on Friday on charges he murdered her.

James Costello, 27, who had been the prime suspect in the shooting death of his mother, Dr. Teresita Valera-Costello, a prominent gynecologist, has been charged with second degree murder, manslaughter and criminal possession of a weapon, Bronx District Attorney Robert Johnson said.
Costello was denied bail in a hearing before Bronx Criminal Judge Faviola Soto after Edward Talty, the assistant district attorney, said the defendant "had access to money and was a flight risk."
The prosecutor said that when Costello's mother discovered her son had been stealing money from her, she confided to relatives that she was going to kick him out of their $1 million mansion.

Valera-Costello, 64, was reported missing by friends on Dec. 10, 1994 after she failed to show up in her native Philippines where she was to have been the keynote speaker at her alma mater, Santa Thomas University. Her plane ticket for a Dec. 6 flight and her passport were found at her home.
Her partially nude body was found on Jan. 14, 1995 in the trunk of her Mercedes-Benz with two bullets in her head, police said.
Police said the son never reported her missing when she vanished.
"We feel that sufficient proof exists to show that James Costello was the one and only person that caused that death," Johnson said Thursday.
